note: After Sjöstedt's 1914 original description (in German, published under the subgenus Allodontermes of the genus Termes as Termes (Allodontermes) rhodesiensis n. sp.); only the soldier is described. The original was extracted by OCR from an Internet Archive scan; fractions and some letters are damaged (e.g. 2,o=2,0; l,o=1,0) and have been restored from context; fractions that could not be confirmed are not included.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related and larger than T. (Allodontermes) schultzi Silvestri, described from the Kalahari (Jenaische Denkschriften 13: 75, 1908); this species is smaller.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale reddish yellow, short rectangular, about 3/4 as wide as long, scattered with pale hairs; frons with a distinct horn-shaped groove. Labrum ligulate, narrowing forwards, ending in a pale whitish point; mandibles narrowing outwards, the tips incurved, blackish red, pale yellow at the base; the left mandible with an oblique downward incision beyond the middle, the outer edge of the incision with 2 small teeth, the inner side with 3 slightly larger teeth; the right mandible with a deeper and wider incision slightly before the middle, forming a sharp right-angled tooth below; antennae 17-segmented, the basal segment about as long as segments 2 and 3 together, segment 2 about as long as segments 3 and 4, segment 3 smallest, segments 4 and 5 equal in size and slightly smaller than segments 6 and 7, the segments enlarging outwards, the last largest and tapering outwards; pronotum rounded pentagonal, the anterior lobe small and with a longitudinal groove, the middle of the anterior margin distinctly heart-shaped and concave, the posterior margin of the posterior lobe slightly concave with a deep groove along the midline; mesonotum broadly oval, the posterior margin slightly concave; metanotum as wide as the pronotum, the posterior margin broadly rounded. Body and legs pale straw yellow, densely covered with fine hairs. Measurements: body length 3.5—4; head including mandibles 2.0, excluding mandibles 1.40; head width 1.0; mandibles 0.7. Type locality Rhodesia, Salisbury, soldier, collected by G. A. K. Marshall (in the London and Stockholm museums).
